flags.headline: US-Iran conflict escalates further overnight — cumulative US troop toll now reported at 17, 9th straight night of strikes, Brent briefly topped $90/bbl
flags.detail: As of Monday 07-20 pre-market, President Trump said Iran has been 'very, very badly damaged' militarily and signaled operations will continue; CENTCOM confirmed a 9th consecutive night of US strikes aimed at protecting Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes. Cumulative reported US troop deaths now stand at 17. Brent crude briefly surpassed $90/bbl overnight before easing to $88.54 (+0.50%); WTI eased slightly to $82.35 (-0.17%). Equity index futures were nonetheless higher pre-market (SPY +0.22%, QQQ +0.40%), suggesting the market is reading the strikes as contained rather than escalatory toward a broader regional war. This remains a portfolio-wide macro development rather than a single-name thesis break: a continuing tailwind for the energy sleeve (VLO, CVX, OKE, DVN, CNX — 5 of 52 holdings) and a standing geopolitical overhang for risk sentiment broadly.

flags.headline: MARA persisting RED — Morgan Stanley cuts price target to $5.50 (from $7), keeps Underweight, ahead of Monday's open
flags.detail: No new equity session yet since Friday's -6.47% close ($11.44->$10.70). Morgan Stanley cut its MARA price target to $5.50 from $7 and reiterated an Underweight rating, a fresh bearish catalyst landing over the weekend that compounds the existing two-session ~13% decline. Bitcoin itself is roughly flat/modestly softer since Friday (~$64,246 vs. Friday's ~$63,950-64,769 range) -- the equity weakness is running ahead of the underlying commodity, consistent with derating on fundamentals (revenue up sharply but EBITDA around -$1.09B, negative ROE/ROA, $2B+ long-term debt) rather than a fresh Bitcoin-price shock. Note a competing bullish thread remains outstanding (Citizens' Outperform / $24 PT on the HPC-pivot thesis 07-06) -- the Street is sharply divided, which itself is a signal of elevated uncertainty into the name.
